question: Does having no conjugate points imply some nonpositively curved metric exists?
idea: Conjugate points describe a particular way nearby geodesics can refocus. The manuscript constructs a closed orientable three-manifold with a metric having no conjugate points, yet with no metric of nonpositive sectional curvature at all. This separates existence of the two kinds of geometry on the same underlying manifold.
why: The study of smooth shapes, curvature, and how geometry changes from point to point.

exactClaim: Constructs a closed connected orientable smooth three-manifold that admits a metric without conjugate points but no metric of nonpositive sectional curvature. This answers negatively, already in dimension three, whether the first metric-existence property implies the second. )
